info.name: Bizmitra Tally API — Public Examples
info.description: Public examples for the Bizmitra Tally API. Set key_id, secret, company_id, and application_id after import. Never export or commit personal values. Authentication uses Bearer {{key_id}}:{{secret}}.

request.description:
Push a Tally-ready invoice payload to the sync bridge.

Sends an invoice straight through to the sync bridge — Bizmitra stores nothing on this path. The `invoice` body uses the UNIFIED voucher shape: nested `gst`, `inventory_entries[]` (each with its income `accounting_allocations`), and `ledger_entries[]` that INCLUDES the party line (`is_party: true`, negative tax-inclusive amount). GST is not auto-computed — the party amount must equal −(item + tax lines). The legacy shape (`voucherType`/`order_date`/`customer_name`/`invtotal`/`invoice_items`/`invoice_ledgers`/flat `gst_*`) is still accepted; unified keys win if both are sent. `request_type` sets the direction: `in` = import into Tally (default), `out` = export. A server-generated `transaction_id` is returned for correlating status callbacks. Watch the date formats — see the payload schema.

Push a Tally-ready Sales Order payload to the sync bridge.

The order sibling of `Sync invoice`: same path, same auth, same UNIFIED body (keyed `order` instead of `invoice`) — nested `gst`, `inventory_entries[]` with `accounting_allocations`, and `ledger_entries[]` including the party line. Order-only: `voucher_type` is `Sales Order` and a top-level `reference` is REQUIRED; set `order_no`/`order_due_date` on a batch for Tally order-tracking. Legacy keys (`voucherType`/`order_date`/`customer_name`/`invoice_items`/`invoice_ledgers`/flat `gst_*`) are still accepted; unified keys win. Bizmitra stores nothing on this path. `request_type` sets the direction (`in` default / `out`). A server-generated `transaction_id` is returned for correlating status callbacks.

Push a credit note (invoice-shaped, positive magnitudes) to Tally.

Trading voucher — same invoice-shaped body as `Sync invoice` (items + party + tax lines under `voucher`), sent as POSITIVE magnitudes; the endpoint applies the credit-note direction (party credited, items/taxes debited). You never encode the signs. Body accepted under `voucher` (primary) or `invoice` (alias — a pulled payload pushes straight back). `event_type` defaults to `credit_note_create`. Poll status with `job_type=credit_note_sync`, then pair on `tally_voucher_guid`.

Push a debit note (invoice-shaped) to Tally.

Trading voucher — same invoice-shaped body as `Sync invoice`, sent as POSITIVE magnitudes; the endpoint applies the debit-note direction (party debited, items/taxes positive — same sides as a sales invoice). Body under `voucher` (or `invoice`). `event_type` defaults to `debit_note_create`. Poll status with `job_type=debit_note_sync`.

Push a purchase voucher (invoice-shaped) to Tally.

Trading voucher — same invoice-shaped body as `Sync invoice`, sent as POSITIVE magnitudes; the endpoint applies the purchase direction (party credited, items/taxes debited). Point the item's `accounting_allocations` at your PURCHASE/expense ledger (e.g. "Local Purchase"). Body under `voucher` (or `invoice`). `event_type` defaults to `purchase_create`. Poll status with `job_type=purchase_sync`.

Push a receipt voucher (ledger_entries + is_debit) to Tally.

Accounting voucher — no inventory header. The body is just `ledger_entries[]`, each line carrying its own direction via `is_debit` (bank/cash debited, party credited). Mark the party/bank line `is_party`. Body under `voucher` (or `invoice`). `event_type` defaults to `receipt_create`. Poll status with `job_type=receipt_sync`.

Push a payment voucher (ledger_entries + is_debit, optional cheque) to Tally.

Accounting voucher — `ledger_entries[]` with per-line `is_debit` (expense/party debited, bank/cash credited). A bank line may carry `bank_allocations[]` for cheque / transfer details (`transaction_type` is REQUIRED for the allocation to be emitted). Body under `voucher` (or `invoice`). `event_type` defaults to `payment_create`. Poll status with `job_type=payment_sync`.

Push a contra voucher (bank ↔ bank / cash) to Tally.

Accounting voucher — `ledger_entries[]` with per-line `is_debit`: one bank/cash debited, the other credited. Each bank line may carry `bank_allocations[]`. Body under `voucher` (or `invoice`). `event_type` defaults to `contra_create`. Poll status with `job_type=contra_sync`.

Push a journal voucher (balanced ledger_entries, optional stock) to Tally.

Accounting voucher — `ledger_entries[]` per your double-entry, each line with `is_debit`; the lines MUST balance. A ledger line may carry `inventory_allocations[]` to track stock against it (stock journal). Body under `voucher` (or `invoice`). `event_type` defaults to `journal_create`. Poll status with `job_type=journal_sync`.

query.description: Exact match on your push reference — omit for all.

request.description:
Poll the status of your pushed invoices/orders — completed, still pending, or failed with the reason.

The READ side of `Sync invoice` / `Sync sales order` (symmetric to `List master jobs`). Lists your voucher-sync jobs and where each one is: a stuck job shows `pending`/`reserved`, a broken one `failed`/`dead_letter` with the Tally error. Filters (all optional): `transaction_id` (exact — look up one push by your own reference), `job_type` (`invoice_sync` | `order_sync` — omit for both), `company_id` (one of your company `id`s), `status` (`pending` | `reserved` | `completed` | `failed` | `dead_letter`), `since_id`, `limit` (≤200), `offset`. Use `Get transaction status` for one job's pushed payload + raw Tally reply. Nothing is stored in Bizmitra; the job store lives behind the sync bridge.

variable.description: Path parameter — fill in before sending.

request.description:
One sync job in full — status, the payload you pushed, and the raw Tally response.

Returns the same record as the list item PLUS `payload` (the voucher body you pushed) and `tally_response_xml` (Tally's raw reply — the place to read a rejection). `{job}` is the `job_id` from `Sync invoice`/`Sync sales order` or the list endpoint. Scoped to your developer account, so a job outside your scope returns not-found.

query.description: PREFERRED — coarse standard kind (snake_case): sales, sales_order, purchase, purchase_order, payment, receipt, contra, journal, debit_note, credit_note, stock_journal, delivery_note, receipt_note, other. Matches custom/renamed types (e.g. "Mumbai Sales" → sales). Omit for all.
Exact Tally type name (may be custom, e.g. "Mumbai Sales"). Precise single-type match only — prefer voucher_kind.
Inclusive start of the voucher-date window (YYYY-MM-DD).
Inclusive end of the voucher-date window (YYYY-MM-DD).
Free-text search over voucher number + party/narration.
Sort field: end_date (voucher date, default) | start_date | voucher_number | received_at.
Page size (max 500). Ordered by voucher date, newest first, by default.

request.description:
Poll for ANY Tally-originated vouchers waiting to be consumed — filter by voucher_kind (metadata only, no XML).

The inverse of the push side: lists ALL voucher types your customer's paired Connector pushed up from Tally. This is ONE type-neutral endpoint — narrow it with a filter rather than calling a per-type URL.

**Filter by `voucher_kind`, not `voucher_type`.** In Tally, `voucher_type` is the EXACT type name and is user-customizable — a company may name its sales voucher `Mumbai Sales` or `Sales Auto Voucher`, so filtering on the literal string silently misses custom types. `voucher_kind` is a COARSE, standard kind (snake_case) the Connector derives for every row: `sales`, `sales_order`, `purchase`, `purchase_order`, `payment`, `receipt`, `contra`, `journal`, `debit_note`, `credit_note`, `stock_journal`, `delivery_note`, `receipt_note`, `other`. It matches custom/renamed types (`Mumbai Sales` → `sales`), so `voucher_kind=sales` returns every sales voucher regardless of its display name.

Params: `company_id` (REQUIRED — one of your company `id`s; poll each company separately), `voucher_kind` (PREFERRED — from the list above), `voucher_type` (exact name; precise single-type match only), `status` (default `pending`), `start_date`/`end_date` (inclusive voucher-date window, e.g. `2026-03-01`), `voucher_number` (exact-or-partial match), `q` (free-text search over voucher number / party / narration), `sort` (`end_date` | `start_date` | `voucher_number` | `received_at`) + `order` (`asc` | `desc`), `limit` (≤500), `offset`. Rows come back ordered by `end_date` desc (newest first) unless you override `sort`/`order`.

**[beta] Filtering is connector-side.** `start_date`, `end_date`, `voucher_number`, `q`, `sort` and `order` are forwarded to the pull bridge and only take effect where the connector supports them; against an older connector they are ignored (you get the unfiltered, default-ordered page). `company_id`, `status`, `voucher_kind`, `voucher_type`, `limit` and `offset` always apply. Each row carries both `voucher_type` (exact) and `voucher_kind` (coarse). Nothing is stored in Bizmitra. The response array is keyed `invoices` but contains EVERY voucher type. (Replaces the old `pulled-invoices`/`pulled-orders` names — those routes still resolve.)

variable.description: Path parameter — fill in before sending.

request.description:
Fetch one pulled voucher (any type) with its full Tally XML.

Returns the complete record for one pulled voucher of ANY type, including `invoice_xml` (and `print_xml` when present) — the actual Tally voucher to consume. The `invoice`/`invoice_xml` keys are historical wire names; the record holds any voucher type (its `voucher_type` says which). Requires `company_id` (your DeveloperCompany id) as a query param. `{transaction_id}` is the `transaction_id` from the list endpoint; rows are scoped to your developer account + company, so a transaction_id outside your company simply returns not-found.

Mark pulled vouchers (any type) consumed so they stop returning as pending.

Flips the given rows `pending` → `synced` regardless of voucher type. Requires `company_id` (your DeveloperCompany id) and `transaction_ids` — a non-empty array of the `transaction_id`s returned by the list endpoint. Idempotent: acking an already-synced row is a no-op. This closes the poll → fetch → ack loop.

query.description: Pin one snapshot: "current" or a Tally yyyymmdd. Omit for the live row.

request.description:
Closing qty/rate/amount per item — the all-items snapshot the connector pushes on a timer.

Reads the all-items closing-stock snapshot for one company (the connector pushes it on its own cadence — no request needed). Params: `company_id` (REQUIRED — your DeveloperCompany id), `as_of_date` (Tally yyyymmdd, or `current`; omit for the live row), `limit`/`offset`. Numbers come back parsed (`closing_qty_number`/`closing_rate`/`closing_amount`); `closing_qty` keeps the raw text with its unit. Values can be negative; qty may be null for amount-only items.

Each row also carries `item_guid` + `parent_guid` (link to its node in `GET /api/v1/stock-tree` — rename-safe; null until the item's masters are pulled), plus provenance `refresh_reason` (`initial` | `change` | `timer`) and `source`. Terminal in Flask — nothing is stored in Bizmitra.

query.description: REQUIRED — Exact Tally stock item name.

request.description:
Read one item's 12-month in/out/closing summary.

Reads the stored monthly summary for one item — all 12 months of the financial year. The connector auto-pulls stock drill-downs, so no request step is needed; just read. Params: `company_id` (REQUIRED), `item_name` (REQUIRED), `range_key` (`from:to` or `current`). Numbers parsed alongside the raw text.

Nested stock-group hierarchy (arbitrary depth), built from the stock masters.

Reads the company's stock-group hierarchy as a nested tree (`children` recurses to any depth). Params: `company_id` (REQUIRED). Each node has `guid` (stable, rename-safe), `name`, `kind` (`group` | `item`), `parent_guid` (null at root — Tally's implicit Primary), and Tally's OWN `closing_qty` / `closing_value` (no self-rollup; group `closing_qty` is null when it mixes units). Join a `stock-summary` item to its node via `item_guid`, then walk `parent_guid` up to the root for the full chain.

Built from the stock MASTERS, not the flat Stock Summary report — so a POPULATED tree needs BOTH the `report.stock` grant AND `pull.master` (the masters the tree is assembled from). With `report.stock` but not `pull.master`, this returns an EMPTY tree (`node_count: 0`), not an error. Terminal in Flask — nothing is stored in Bizmitra.

query.description: REQUIRED — Exact Tally stock item name.

request.description:
Read one item's voucher-wise movement over a range.

Reads the stored voucher-wise movement for one item over a date range. The connector auto-pulls stock drill-downs, so no request step is needed; just read. Params: `company_id` (REQUIRED), `item_name` (REQUIRED), `range_key` (`from:to`). Each row carries date/party/voucher_type/voucher_number and parsed inwards/outwards numbers.

query.description: "from:to" or "current" (almost always "current" — the report ignores dates).

request.description:
Read the stored month-by-month funds flow (opening / closing / funds flow).

Reads the stored monthly funds flow for one company. The connector auto-pulls it on a timer (like stock) — no request step, just read. Params: `company_id` (REQUIRED), `range_key` (`from:to` or `current` — almost always `current`, since the report ignores dates). Always 12 rows (April..March); unposted months come back with null amounts but a real `period`. `*_number` fields are parsed numbers; Tally Dr balances are signed negative — take `abs()` to match the on-screen figure. Terminal in Flask — nothing is stored in Bizmitra.

Enqueue a Profit & Loss A/c pull; read it back after the connector polls.

Enqueues a Profit & Loss pull for one company; the paired Connector runs it on its next poll, then read via `GET /api/v1/profit-loss`. Async — returns a `job_id`. Body: `company_id` (REQUIRED), `transaction_id` (optional idempotency key). NB: the report IGNORES the date window — it always returns the FULL company period; single-month P&L via export is not possible. Needs the `report.financials` capability.

Read the stored Profit & Loss A/c line items (full company period).

Reads the stored P&L line items for one company (trigger it first via `POST /api/v1/profit-loss/refresh`). Params: `company_id` (REQUIRED), `range_key` (`current`). Two-column layout: each line has EITHER `sub_amount` (a sub-line like Opening/Closing Stock) OR `main_amount` (a main total like Sales / Cost of Sales), not both; `*_number` fields are parsed. Full company period only — the date window is ignored. Terminal in Flask — nothing is stored in Bizmitra.

query.description: "current" or a Tally yyyymmdd. Omit for the live row.
Narrow to one TDS ledger. Omit for all.

request.description:
Per-party TDS-outstanding snapshot the connector pushes on a timer.

Reads the per-party TDS-payable snapshot for one company (the connector pushes it on its own cadence — no request needed). Params: `company_id` (REQUIRED — your DeveloperCompany id), `as_of_date` (Tally yyyymmdd or `current`; omit for the live row), `tds_ledger` (narrow to one TDS ledger), `limit`/`offset` (default 500, max 2000). `closing_amount`/`*_number` are parsed numbers. NB: the per-party split only exists when the TDS ledger is bill-by-bill with deductee-tagged entries — otherwise a single `party = "On Account"` bucket is returned. The snapshot is upserted, not pruned: a fully-paid party stops being sent but its last row is NOT deleted — use `updated_at`/`as_of_date` for freshness. Terminal in Flask — nothing stored in Bizmitra.

Enqueue a bill-wise TDS pull for one party under a TDS ledger.

Enqueues a bill-wise TDS breakup for ONE party; the paired Connector runs it on its next poll (~seconds), then read via `GET /api/v1/tds/bills`. Async — returns a `job_id`. Body: `company_id` (REQUIRED), `tds_ledger` (REQUIRED), `party` (REQUIRED), `from_date`/`to_date` (Tally yyyymmdd, optional), `transaction_id` (optional idempotency key). A repeat request for the same ledger+party+window REPLACES the stored rows. Needs the `report.tds` capability.

query.description: REQUIRED — Deductee party — get the exact name from GET /api/v1/tds-summary.

request.description:
Read one party's stored bill-wise TDS breakup.

Reads the stored bill-wise TDS breakup for ONE party (trigger it first via `POST /api/v1/tds/bills/refresh`). Params: `company_id` (REQUIRED), `party` (REQUIRED), `tds_ledger` (narrow to one ledger), `range_key` (`from:to` or `current`). Each row carries `bill_date`/`bill_ref`/`due_date` (Tally display strings), `opening`/`closing` (raw text + parsed `*_number`), and `overdue_days`. Terminal in Flask — nothing stored in Bizmitra.

variable.description: Path parameter — fill in before sending.

request.description:
Push a master (single or batch) into the customer’s Tally — the master type is in the URL.

Enqueues a master push for `{type}`; the customer’s paired Connector imports it on its next poll. Returns immediately with a `job_id`. Idempotent on `transaction_id` (a duplicate echoes the original job with `duplicate:true`).

`{type}` is one of the nine registry keys — `group`, `ledger`, `currency`, `unit`, `godown`, `stock_group`, `stock_category`, `stock_item`, `voucher_type` (hyphens accepted: `stock-item` ≡ `stock_item`). The type lives in the URL, so the master body NEVER repeats it.

Body: `company_id` (one of your company `id`s, bound to a connector), `transaction_id` (your idempotency key), `event_type` (`master_create` or `master_alter`), and exactly ONE of `master` (a single object) or `masters` (a list — batch, ordered parents-first: currencies/units/groups/categories before ledgers/stock items). Every master needs `name`; all other fields are optional and type-specific.

Rules: `gst_rate` is a SINGLE percent (e.g. 18) — the connector splits CGST/SGST/IGST; never send separate heads. Without `guid` Tally upserts by `name`. Pair your record on the returned `tally_master_guid` (read `GET /api/v1/masters/{type}`) once `status` is `completed` — push one master per job when you need the GUID back (a batch returns only a LASTMID).

variable.description: Path parameter — fill in before sending.

request.description:
Read the outcome of your master pushes for one type (pair on tally_master_guid).

Lists your master-sync jobs for `{type}` and their outcome. Poll incrementally with `?since_id=<last id seen>`. Params (all optional): `company_id` (one of your company `id`s), `status` (`pending`/`reserved`/`completed`/`failed`/`dead_letter`), `since_id`, `limit` (≤200), `offset`.

Once a row is `completed`, **pair on `tally_master_guid`** — it is stable across renames and re-imports (the numeric `tally_master_id` is per-company; the name can change). For a batch job, `master_name` is null and `masters` lists each `{type,name}`. Use `GET /api/v1/masters/{type}/{job}` for one job’s full detail including the pushed payload.

variable.description: Path parameter — fill in before sending.
Path parameter — fill in before sending.

request.description:
One master job with its full detail, including the payload you pushed.

Returns the same record as the list item PLUS the `payload` (the master body you pushed). `{job}` is the `job_id` from the push/list response. Scoped to your developer account + type, so a job outside your scope simply returns not-found.

Proof endpoint — exercises the full key + company auth stack and echoes your request context.

Use this first to confirm your API key, secret and `X-Bizmitra-Company` header are wired up correctly. It does not touch Tally, so it returns instantly.

variable.description: Path parameter — fill in before sending.

request.description:
Passthrough to the customer’s paired Tally Connector via long-poll dispatch.

**Under development — not available yet.** This live passthrough bridge is not wired to the developer's paired Connector at the moment, so calls currently return `504 connector_timeout`. Use the dedicated push endpoints (invoices/orders/etc.) and the pulled-vouchers read surface instead. When ready: forwards the request body to the paired Connector for the company in `X-Bizmitra-Company` and returns Tally's response; nothing is persisted in Bizmitra.

List your registered applications.

Control-plane (key-only, no company header). Returns the applications registered under your developer account.

query.description: Filter to one customer's companies (their share_token). Omit for all.

request.description:
List your developer companies and their connection state (filter by customer).

Paginated. Each row includes pairing/connector/Tally binding state plus `customer_token` (the customer this company is grouped under, or null). Filter to ONE customer's companies with `customer_token=<share_token>` — a foreign/unknown token returns 404.

List your customers (client groupings) + company counts.

A customer is one of your clients — a grouping key that lets ONE pairing code authorize all of a client's companies (connector tenant isolation). It holds NO contact/PII. Returns the opaque, rotatable `share_token` (your handle for grouping companies), `reference` (your own tag), `status` and `company_count`. The internal id is never exposed.

Create a customer (client grouping). Returns its share_token.

Creates a customer grouping under your account and returns the opaque, rotatable `share_token`. Use it as `customer_token` when creating/grouping companies, then mint ONE pairing code per customer (`Generate pairing code`). Optional `reference` = your own tag (unique per developer). No contact/PII is stored — a customer is only a grouping of companies.

variable.description: Path parameter — fill in before sending.

request.description:
Rotate a customer’s share_token (e.g. on suspected leak).

Issues a new `share_token`; the old one stops working immediately. The customer's identity and ALL its machine grants are untouched (nothing re-pairs). `{token}` is the CURRENT share_token. A token that isn't yours → 404.

Register a developer company under an application (optionally grouped under a customer).

Creates a logical company under one of your applications. Returns its `id` and `uuid`. Optionally pass `customer_token` (from `Create customer`) to group it under a customer (client): if that customer already has a paired machine, the company auto-flows to it (appears in the client's Connector with no re-pairing). A foreign/unknown `customer_token` returns 404.

variable.description: Path parameter — fill in before sending.

request.description:
Group an existing company under a customer (auto-flows to its machine).

Moves an existing company into one of your customers. If that customer already has a paired machine, the company is granted to it immediately — it appears in the client's Connector with NO re-pairing and NO new code. `{id}` = your company id. Body: `customer_token`. A foreign company or customer → 404.

variable.description: Path parameter — fill in before sending.

request.description:
Ungroup a company from its customer (revokes it from the machine).

Removes the company from its customer group. If the customer has a paired machine, the company is revoked from it and its sync stops immediately (no re-pairing). `{id}` = your company id.

Mint a CUSTOMER-scoped pairing code (authorizes all a client’s companies).

Mint ONE pairing code for a customer (client): it authorizes ALL of that customer's companies at once. Body: `customer_token` (REQUIRED — from `Create customer`), `expires_in` optional (default 900s). The client redeems it ONCE and their Connector is locked to exactly those companies — they can never see another client (tenant isolation). Add a company to the customer later and it auto-flows to the paired machine with no new code. The customer must have at least one company (422 otherwise). The plaintext `pairing_code` is returned only here, once.

List your pairing codes and their status.

Lists pairing codes for your account. `status` filter optional: active | used | expired | revoked. `limit`/`offset` optional. Plaintext codes are never re-exposed here — metadata only.

variable.description: Path parameter — fill in before sending.

request.description:
Revoke an unused pairing code.

Revokes an unused code by `{id}`. Returns 400 if it was already used. Regenerate = revoke the old one, then POST a new pairing code.

variable.description: Path parameter — fill in before sending.

request.description:
Check before you sync — is the connector online, is Tally running, is the right company loaded, right now.

Live connector + Tally health for one company in ONE call, so your backend can decide whether a push will land BEFORE sending it (instead of firing blind and reading a `504 connector_timeout` after the fact). `{id}` = your company `id`; key-only auth (no `X-Bizmitra-Company`).

Returns two 4-state machines:

**`tally_status`** — the Tally desktop probe:
- `running` — Tally is open on the paired machine.
- `not_running` — the connector is online, but Tally is closed. *Show your user: "Please open Tally."*
- `reconnecting` — a transient link loss, recovering.
- `unreachable` — connector offline / machine asleep / bridge unavailable. *Show your user: "Connector is offline."*

**`company_status`** — the company-binding probe:
- `company_linked` — the correct company is loaded and bound. Safe to sync.
- `no_company_loaded` — Tally is running but no company is open.
- `company_unavailable` — the company is known but not currently reachable.
- `company_not_linked` — the company isn't bound to this connector.

Always returns HTTP `200` with a usable state — an offline connector or an unreachable bridge degrades to `tally_status=unreachable` + `company_status=company_not_linked` rather than an error, because "don't push yet" IS the answer you need. Unmetered, so you can call it before every sync. `connector_paired` is the stored pairing fact; `connector_online`/`tally_running`/`company_linked` are the live probe. Preflight pattern: call this → if `tally_running` and `company_linked`, push; otherwise surface the state to your user and retry.

variable.description: Path parameter — fill in before sending.

request.description:
Tear down a company’s connection (clears pairing/connector/Tally state).

Mirrors the portal’s Disconnect button — resets the company to `disconnected` and clears its pairing code, connector and Tally-binding snapshots. Call this when a user disconnects from the Connector app. Generate a new pairing code to reconnect.

List the paired Connector machines on your account.

Pairing is account-wide: you pair one Connector per machine (no per-company code) and can own many. Lists each paired machine with device/OS/connector version, online + Tally state, and linked-company count. `include_removed=1` to include removed machines. `online` is derived from heartbeat freshness; `state` is active | disabled | removed.

variable.description: Path parameter — fill in before sending.

request.description:
One Connector machine with its linked companies.

Full detail for one machine by `{machine}` (its `machine_uuid`), including each linked company's binding + sync health. `sync_health`: healthy | syncing | degraded | paused. `company_status`: company_linked | no_company_loaded | company_unavailable | company_not_linked. `tally_status`: running | not_running | reconnecting | unreachable. A machine that isn't yours returns 404.

List your webhook subscriptions and their health.

A webhook subscribes a URL to connector/Tally state transitions — `connector.online` · `connector.offline` · `tally.started` · `tally.stopped` · `company.linked` · `company.unlinked` — so Bizmitra pushes an event to you instead of you polling. Lists your subscriptions with health (`consecutive_failures`, `last_success_at`, whether auto-disabled) and a masked `secret_hint`. The signing secret itself is shown only at create/rotate.

Subscribe a URL to connector/Tally events. Returns the signing secret ONCE.

Registers a webhook. Body: `url` (https), `events` (array — omit or `[]` for ALL of the six event types), `description` (optional), `all_applications` (optional bool — default is to scope to THIS key's application; set true to receive events from every app you own). The response includes the **`secret`** in full — the ONLY time it is returned. Store it: every delivery is signed `X-Bizmitra-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hmac-sha256 of "{t}.{body}">`, so you verify with this secret. Rotate or re-read via the other endpoints (thereafter only a masked `secret_hint` is shown).
